subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support Podman only for local connections and Podman Machine, rejecting arbitrary remote Podman connections in favor of the SSH backend?
rationale: This is an intentional authorization boundary for a new built-in engine with host workspace mounts; source review can verify enforcement, but only maintainers can set the supported threat-model and operations boundary.

options.title: Accept the local/Machine boundary
options.body: Keep the documented fail-closed rule, require refreshed exact-head runtime proof, and proceed through normal merge checks.

options.title: Broaden remote Podman support
options.body: Define and review a separate remote-host security, authentication, and workspace-confinement contract before allowing arbitrary Podman connections.

options.title: Defer the backend
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers do not want to own another built-in container-engine boundary at this time.

recommendation.title: Accept the local/Machine boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the documented fail-closed rule, require refreshed exact-head runtime proof, and proceed through normal merge checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-head refactor and maintainer comment establish direct ownership of the shared sandbox-engine design.
